system.description:
Clerics of Boccob receive this spell when they become able to cast 6th level spells. It is a weaker form of Boccob's own disc of Concordant Opposition. The cleric creates a disc that blasts most creatures into nothingness unless they resist magic.

Creatures with fewer than 6 hit dice or less than 35% magic resistance are destroyed if they fail their save. Creatures with 6 hit dice or more take 75 points of damage if they fail their save. Creatures with 6 or more hit dice take 40 points of damage, saving for half. Any creature with more than 35% magic resistance is unaffected.

The second and third sentences are given as printed; they appear to contradict each other for creatures of 6 or more hit dice.

The cleric must carry Boccob's holy symbol to cast the spell. The material component is a small wheel of iron and electrum with a rod rising from the center of one side. The cleric hurls the disc at the target while finishing a prayer to Boccob.

GA p.6. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates 2-5 (1d4+1) stone spheres, each six inches across, that shoot from the caster's hand in a straight line toward the target or targets the caster picks. They hit unless the target saves vs. spells (dexterity and racial bonuses do not apply), at -2 if the range is 10 yards or less. Each meteor that hits does 1d4+4 damage. The caster may release them one at a time or all at once, but any not released when the spell ends are lost. The material component is Celestian's circle of stars symbol, and the cleric must be under the open sky to cast the spell.

GA p.7. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives the cleric's bronzewood or oak cudgel the power to charm an opponent by touch. The cleric may try a harmless touch or a normal melee attack; either way, a target that is hit must save vs. spells or be charmed. If the cleric makes a damaging attack, though, each point of damage from the hit gives the target +1 on the save (a roll of 1 always fails).

A charmed creature sees the cleric as a comrade, friend or teacher, treats him or her with love and respect, and trusts the cleric completely. If they can communicate, it obeys as well as it can, as long as the instructions seem reasonable and do not plainly lead to needless harm, loss or a breach of its alignment. The charm lasts 2d10 rounds. The spell is especially good for getting the incorrigible to listen to the teachings of St. Cuthbert or to give to worthy causes.

Used together with shillelagh, the victim saves at -1. The magic lasts three rounds plus one round per level of the caster, or until the cleric hits with the cudgel, whichever comes first.

GA p.9. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell makes its recipient almost invisible in natural surroundings and almost completely silent, as if wearing a cloak and boots of elvenkind, and almost completely hides his or her scent. While the recipient stays still, nothing non-magical can detect him or her beyond 30 feet. Moving does not end the spell, but it makes non-magical detection possible. The spell ends when its duration runs out or when the recipient attacks. The material components are Ehlonna's unicorn horn symbol and a piece of dried chameleon skin.

GA p.10. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This special curse makes any journey longer than one league (three miles) take twice as long as normal. The victim drags his feet, wanders in circles or crooked lines, insists on long rests, and does (or fails to do) other things that lengthen the distance, slow the travel, or both. Any mount the victim rides is affected the same way.

The only cures are remove curse cast by a cleric of higher level than the original caster, or waiting for the duration to run out. The material components are Fharlanghn's holy symbol (a disc with a curved line) and a pinch of road dust or damp mud.

GA p.11. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell lets the cleric strike a single target with a virulent, infectious disease. If the target saves vs. spells, nothing happens. If not, the target at once suffers an attack of plague, feverish and confused with illness for six turns. During that time the victim loses 10% of his original hit points and one point each of strength and constitution, suffers -2 on saving throws and hit rolls, and is hit at +2.

Every creature (and character) within 10 feet of the victim must pass a constitution check or catch the plague too. A creature already sick with it cannot catch it again, and one near more than one victim checks only once.

When the attack ends, so do the penalties, but lost hit points and ability points take 1d6 days to return. Before the effects wear off there is one last attack: the victim must make a constitution check against his lowered score. If it fails, the victim dies; if he survives, the lost hit points and ability points return.

GA p.12. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a mass of weak, sticky threads lasting one turn. They block sight but not movement, cannot be burned, and can be removed only by a successful dispel magic. Any creature touching them must save vs. spells at -3 or be teleported at once into a misty maze of unlimited size. Prisoners there are filled with nameless dread, can see only 10 feet, and have a 50% chance of attacking any creature they meet, friend or foe. Prisoners not in combat may save vs. spells on the second round and each round after until they escape or the spell ends.

A creature with magic resistance rolls when it touches the threads; if it succeeds it is not caught, and if it fails it is trapped until it saves or the spell ends. Prisoners still in the maze when the spell ends return to where they started.

GA p.14. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell lets the cleric produce a disgusting spittle that paralyzes whatever it touches. The cleric makes a hit roll, with every target counted as at short range. A creature struck must save vs. spells or lose the use of the part hit:

d8Area struckEffect
1HeadUnconscious
2-4BodyParalyzed
5Weapon armNo attacks
6Non-weapon armNo shield bonus
7-8LegLoses defensive dexterity bonuses; movement halved

All effects last 1d4+1 rounds. The DM may change the hit location table to allow for which way the target is facing or a body that is not humanlike.

GA p.15. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell summons a lump of blackness five feet across with four 10-foot arms reaching out from it at right angles. Touching the central lump causes death unless a save vs. death is made. The arms attack with the casting cleric's chance to hit, doing d10+2 points of corrosion and crushing damage. A creature struck gets one chance to break free, equal to its chance to open doors. If that is unknown, assume creatures smaller than man-sized escape on 1 on 1d6, man-sized on 1-2, and larger on 1-3.

The round after an arm hits, it pulls back into the central lump, and the victim in its grip must save vs. death. After that the victim is held fast and keeps taking corrosion and crushing damage, but further contact with the lump calls for no more saves vs. death. Broken arms pull back into the lump without attacking again. Arms holding dead creatures keep holding them until the spell ends.

The material components are Nerull's unholy symbol (the skull and scythe) and a small, rusty iron ball.

GA p.16. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a brilliant flash of golden light. Undead in the area take 6d6 damage (no save). All other creatures in the burst, or facing it, must save vs. spells or be blinded for 2-12 segments. Creatures without eyes, or not sensitive to visible light, are unaffected. A sunburst cancels darkness spells in its area if they were cast by someone of the same or lower level than the cleric. The material components are Pholtus' silvery sun holy symbol and a bead of any clear crystal.

GA p.17. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell lets the cleric bend fate, at some risk. Whenever the cleric faces a situation of chance, he or she need only make the spell's mystic gestures to add +10% to the die roll (compare stone of good luck). But each use has a 5% chance (not cumulative) of backfiring and producing the worst possible result for the caster.

Applied to a saving throw, the spell gives +2 to the roll (a 1 always fails), but on a natural 20 disaster strikes and the cleric takes maximum damage from the attack.

The cleric must be alive to use the spell and must display Ralishaz's holy symbol of three bones openly.

GA p.18. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives the cleric limited power over creatures of elemental earth. While it lasts, earth elementals and other creatures of the Elemental Plane of Earth cannot come within five feet of the caster or attack him or her. The caster may give up this protection to try to charm such a creature, which saves at -2; if the charm fails, the creature is free to attack. While the spell lasts the caster can talk with earth elemental creatures, and those of the cleric's alignment tend to be friendly (unless a charm is attempted). A charmed earth elemental can be used to move earth, as the 6th level magic-user spell. The material components are Ulaa's holy symbol (a mountain with a ruby heart) and an opaque gem.

GA p.19. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell hunts down and destroys one of the mage's most feared enemies, the bookworm. It creates a disembodied hand that searches a library and crushes every bookworm it finds. The hand searches 100 books or scrolls per round, with a 95% chance of finding any bookworm there. Once it finds one, it chases it relentlessly, attacking with the skill of a fighter of the caster's level; any hit crushes the bookworm to death at once. The hand has strength 8, enough to push books and scrolls aside to chase a fleeing worm. Physical attacks cannot harm it, but four or more points of magical damage destroy it. It can do nothing else and fight nothing else. The material component is a child-sized glove of tough leather.

GA p.51. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell calls up a disembodied hand that obeys the caster. It cannot hold, grip or carry anything, but its sense of touch is so astonishingly fine that it can feel tiny cracks, gaps or openings in a surface, and so finds secret or concealed doors with a 50% chance. It searches a 10 foot by 10 foot area each turn. Physical attacks cannot destroy it, but four or more points of magical damage dispel it. It can set off a non-magical trap if the trap's location is known. The material components are a child-sized silk glove and a swan's feather.

GA p.51. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell summons a pair of disembodied hands that follow the mage's every order. They can do anything an unseen servant can, and also tasks needing fine coordination, such as tinkering with tools, working laboratory equipment, sculpting, painting or playing an instrument. They can do any task the caster can, including the mage's non-weapon proficiencies, with the caster's dexterity.

Each hand can hold and carry up to 200 gp weight, or 500 gp weight together, and they can be no farther apart than the caster's own hands. They move 120 feet per round whatever they carry, but vanish if they go more than 90 feet from the caster. They cannot perform the gestures of a spell, wield a weapon in melee, punch or grapple. They are immune to physical attacks but are destroyed by six or more points of magical damage. The material component is a pair of gloves embroidered with the mage's initials.

GA p.51. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a hand of the right size that flies at the chosen creature and clamps tightly over its mouth unless it makes its saving throw. An affected creature cannot speak clearly, cast spells with a verbal component, or use a magic item worked by a spoken command word. The hand cannot be pulled away or harmed by physical attacks, but six or more points of magical damage destroy it, though most magical attacks risk hurting the creature too. A successful dispel magic destroys the hand without harming the creature. The material component is a cloth glove smeared with sticky syrup or honey.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a pair of man-sized hands shaped like clenched, padded fists. They pummel as a fighter with 18/50 strength and half the caster's level. Together they fight as a character with AC 4 and 3 hit points per level of the mage, and are dispelled when their hit points run out. They can only pummel, not hold a weapon or grapple, and they cannot be grappled or overborne, since they easily dart away. The material components are a mitten stuffed with cotton and a brass bell.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a shimmering violet force shaped like a battering ram with a clenched fist for its head: a cylinder 12 feet long and 2 feet across, which the caster can shorten to 3 feet to fit a cramped space.

It works as a very powerful battering ram, smashing a normal door in one hit, a reinforced door in three, and a stone door in five, with a 50% chance of destroying a metal door (if it fails, the spell is destroyed). Like any ram, it makes only one attack per round. Against a smaller obstacle reinforced with magic, such as a dungeon door or metal grate, the door saves at the level of the mage who cast the reinforcing spell; if it saves, the gauntlet is destroyed, and if not, the gauntlet goes to work on it.

The ram has no effect on living targets. The caster must stay within 60 feet of it or it fades away. Physical attacks cannot damage it, but magical damage equal to half the caster's hit points destroys it, as do dispel magic and disintegrate. It cannot open chests or batter anything but a door, and works only on portals meant to open at some time. The material component is a metal rod with a chain mail gauntlet slipped over one end.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates one pair of hands per level of the caster, all equipped with carpentry tools. They work as a crew as able as any team of professional carpenters, masons, miners or sappers, and never need to rest or eat; each pair does the work of one worker. They cannot fight or do physical damage to anything. Nothing non-magical can destroy them, and each pair has as many hit points as the caster has levels. The material components include an assortment of miniature tools worth at least 500 gp.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This very flexible spell lets the mage create a visible sheet of force that can be shaped into any form: a table, ladder, club, bucket, stilts or cane, for example. Once formed, the object keeps its shape for the spell's duration. It must be fairly rigid, with no moving parts, no sharp point or edge, and no fine detail, so a rope, long bow, sword, chariot or accurate statue cannot be made. Objects of force cannot be harmed by physical attacks, but magical attacks doing more damage than the creator's hit points dispel them. Up to one cubic foot of matter per level of the caster can be imitated. The material component is a lump of soft clay mixed with diamond dust.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates one hand for every three levels of the caster, each holding a long sword and fighting with the skill of a fighter of half the caster's level. Being small and quick, each hand is AC 2, and each can take 15 points of damage before being dispelled. A fencer can disarm an opponent, doing so on a roll four higher than it needs to hit; a fencer that is itself disarmed is dispelled at once. The caster need not concentrate to keep them working, only give them orders as if they were henchmen. The material component is a small silver amulet shaped like a mailed gauntlet holding a gem-studded sword, worth at least 1,000 gp, which vanishes when the spell is cast.

GA p.52. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This is a more advanced form of the 4th level force sculpture. The objects formed can be more complex, with large moving parts or an edge or point, though they must still be fairly rigid: a wagon, a quiver of quarrels, a shovel, a sword or a water wheel, but not a mechanical clock, a crossbow or a spring. Fine detail can be added if the caster is skilled enough as an artisan or sculptor; it takes 2d4 rounds to add and lasts for the spell's duration. Up to 8 cubic feet of matter per level of the caster can be imitated, and the spell lasts longer than force sculpture; otherwise it is the same. The material component is a lump of clay mixed with diamond dust.

GA p.53. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a pair of disembodied hands that go for a creature's throat and strangle it, with the same effect as a garrote attack. They need a successful attack roll to seize the throat, using the mage's normal attack roll at +4 because of their speed and ferocity. The grip strangles its victim to death by the end of the next round unless the creature is freed. The victim can break the grip with a successful bend bars roll, and it also lets go if the mage's concentration is broken. The creatures this spell can affect are limited in the same way as those a normal garrote can be used on. The material components are a pair of gloves sewn into a clutching grip around the neck of a bottle.

GA p.53. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

system.duration: 1 round per 2 levels of the spellcaster
system.description:
This spell is similar to magic missile. The mage can fire one magical siege bolt for every two levels, each acting as a particular siege engine missile in range and effect. Which one depends on the caster's level:

Magic-user's levelSiege engine missile copied
12thcatapult, light
14thcatapult, heavy
16thtrebuchet

The bolts must be launched one every two rounds, in succession, and the caster can do nothing else meanwhile. If the spell is interrupted, no more bolts can be launched. The bolts never miss. The material component is a small stone sprinkled with diamond dust.

GA p.53. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This is the most advanced of the force sculpture spells. The object formed can be very complex, with many moving parts, such as a siege engine or a sailing ship, and parts can be as flexible as rope or the wood of a bow, so a large net, a ballista, a rope bridge or a set of crossbows could be made. As with the lesser spells, fine or accurate detail takes another 2d4 rounds and enough skill as an artist or artisan. Up to one cubic yard of matter per level of the caster can be imitated. Apart from these differences it is the same as the 4th level spell. The material component is a lump of clay mixed with 1,000 gp worth of diamond dust, which vanishes when the spell is used.

GA p.53. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell partly lightens the load on a single mount. Everything it carries, riders included, counts as half its weight, in effect doubling what the mount can carry.

A mount suddenly left carrying one and a half times its maximum load without the spell cannot walk, slowly sinks to the ground, and has a 50% chance of going lame. One suddenly left with twice its maximum load collapses, takes 1d6 damage and goes lame automatically.

The material components are a lodestone and a pinch of metal filings.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives a creature a very limited kind of levitation. It walks normally over any surface, but so lightly that it leaves no tracks. If it breaks into a charge or a run, the spell ends at once.

The creature can also walk on liquid as well as solid ground, though at half its normal walking rate, since it must step carefully. It cannot cross rough water or ocean waves, whose wild motion upsets the levitation. It cannot set off pit traps. It cannot jump higher or leap safely from a cliff; it only walks more lightly. The spell also increases the creature's movement rate by 50 percent while it lasts. The material components are a bit of fur from a cat's paw and a duck's feather.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell grants the creature touched a special kind of luck: for its duration, the recipient acts as if holding a luckstone and using its magic. The material component is 5,000 gp worth of ruby dust sprinkled over the creature's head, which vanishes when the spell ends.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives one or more creatures the endurance to hold their breath for five full turns, during which they cannot drown or be affected by inhaled gases. The caster can affect one creature per level. The spell is a single word, with no gestures or material components, so the mage can cast it quickly in an emergency.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell hides every smell coming from a creature for its duration. Cast on the mage or another person, that person cannot be found by scent and cannot be tracked by any animal or being that tracks by smell, such as a bloodhound. Cast on a creature that uses its smell as a weapon or defense, it cancels the smell if the creature fails a save vs. spells; it could stop the musk of a skunk or wolverine or the stench of a troglodyte. The material component is a flower with no scent.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell doubles the movement rate of any mount that runs, swims or flies, for its duration. When it ends, the mount is completely exhausted and refuses to go any farther for 24 hours. The spell does not increase what the mount can carry; its maximum load is unchanged, and overloading it cancels the spell at once. Beast of burden cannot be combined with swift mount to increase a racing mount's load. The material component is a hare's foot or a bit of cheetah fur.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This is an improved version of the 1st level shield spell. It protects the caster against attacks from every side, including behind and above, as long as the mage is aware of the attack; a surprise attack dispels it completely. Its protection is -2 against all attacks: it acts as AC 0 against hand-hurled missiles, AC 1 against missiles from devices, and gives -2 to the mage's armor class against all other attacks.

GA p.54. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell protects the contents of one ordinary sack or backpack as if its inside were lined with solid steel an inch thick, though it becomes no heavier or stiffer. The sack saves against physical or magical damage as hard metal, with a further +2, and items inside need to save only if the sack fails. The material component is a strip of leather with mail sewn to one side.

GA p.55. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell times the next spell the same caster casts. A small golden gong appears in front of the caster and chimes softly one minute before that spell ends. It works only with spells lasting less than 48 hours.

To cast it, the mage must gather a feather from a migrating bird, a fruit fly, a few grains of sand, a solid silver pendulum worth 100 gp and a solid gold orb of exquisite workmanship worth 5,000 gp, all of which vanish when the spell ends.

GA p.55. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives the mage and others a limited, risky kind of teleportation. A door suddenly appears on a wall or other flat surface within 3 yards of the caster. The caster and as many others as can get through it in one round (usually one creature or person per segment) step through into a zone of nil-space. When the mage closes the door behind them, everyone in the nil-space is teleported to a random spot within 250 yards of the door. If the door is not closed before the spell's duration ends, it slams shut by itself at the end of that round. The door vanishes once the mage closes it or it shuts itself.

The party has no control over where they arrive, and there is always a 5% chance the spell goes wrong and drops them on the Ethereal Plane. To decide where they go, the DM traces back along the party's route on the map and places them at a random spot where they have already been; the spell cannot send them into unknown territory. The material component is a miniature silver door decorated with ruby chips, worth 5,000 gp, which vanishes when the spell is cast.

GA p.55. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell creates a sphere 20 feet in radius around the caster in which all creatures are protected from all non-magical gases, fumes and smoke. Natural gases touching the edge of the sphere are dispersed. The air inside stays clean and fresh, always supplied with oxygen, so those inside will not suffocate even if the air outside is fouled or its oxygen burned away by fire. The spell does not work under water or in a vacuum. The sphere moves with the caster, and is dispelled if magical gases touch it or the caster moves by magical means. The material components are a fan and a small vial of perfume worth at least 100 gp, both of which vanish when the spell is cast.

GA p.55. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This handy spell lets the mage call up one to ten tools when needed, totaling up to 200 gp of encumbrance. The caster can keep swapping items for new ones throughout the duration: a hammer and chisel in the first round, a saw in the fifth, a pry bar in the eighth, and so on. Only non-living things can be conjured. The tools cannot be taken more than 100 yards from the box, which cannot be moved, and only the caster can take tools from it.

Only things a carpenter or builder might own can come from the box. Not thieves' tools, wax key blanks, ball bearings, magic weapons or gem cutters' blades; but a skilled carpenter's box might hold rope, a skeleton key, huge hammers and metal stakes, large canvas sheets, nets and sand.

The material component is a miniature wooden tool box.

GA p.55. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This special flying spell is cast on an object, not a creature. The object gains the power to fly up to 180 feet per round as the caster directs: a broom, chair, table, carpet, wagon or hut could all be made to fly. The mage can affect up to 500 gp weight per level, and the object can carry twice that in passengers or freight if it is big and strong enough to hold that weight normally; an 18th level mage could lift a boat weighing 9,000 gp with up to 18,000 gp of cargo, for example. The caster must concentrate on the object to steer it and keep it aloft. If the caster is knocked out, stunned or killed while steering, the object falls like any falling object. The material component is a wing feather from a roc.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives the willing creature touched all the benefits of polymorph self, with no system shock roll needed. The caster chooses its first form, but after that the creature has full control of its changes for the rest of the duration and may change as often as it likes, within all the limits of polymorph self. It gains no special abilities of the forms it takes, and its mind is not affected in any way. When it returns to its own form, it regains 1d12 hit points.

The material component is a soft silk caterpillar cocoon.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell was devised as a merciful way to be rid of an enemy. It polymorphs an opponent into another creature like polymorph other, but the target saves at -2, and can only become a natural animal no larger than a typical herd beast. No system shock roll is needed. The victim automatically takes on the animal's mind, forgetting everything about its former self, and the animal gives off no magic and no trace of the creature's original alignment, so there is little sign it was ever anything else.

If returned to its own form by dispel magic or a wish, the creature is badly bewildered, suffering the effect of confusion for 2d4 rounds, and then slowly regains its knowledge and memories over 1d4 days. The material components are a cocoon soaked in honey balm, powdered yellow-white moss agate worth 500 gp and powdered emerald worth 700 gp, all of which vanish when the spell is cast.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

A creature protected by this spell gains an edge in combat against birds and bird creatures totaling no more than 15 hit dice: they suffer -2 to hit it for the spell's duration. If more hit dice than that attack, the spell is cancelled. The material component is a feather from any bird wrapped in a strip of tough leather.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives a creature full 360 degree vision, so it sees to its sides and rear as well as to its front, and cannot be surprised from behind by any attacker it could see normally. It works with any enhanced or magical sight, including infravision, ultravision or X-ray vision; a creature with both detect invisibility and this spell can also see invisible, ethereal or astral beings at its flanks and rear. The recipient suffers -2 on all saving throws against gas attacks. The material component is a crystal disc with eight eyes inscribed around its edge, 45 degrees apart.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell helps a creature survive attacks by lycanthropes. They suffer -2 to hit it, and however much damage they do, it will not catch lycanthropy while the spell lasts. It gives no protection against lycanthropy from wounds taken before the spell was cast or after it ends. The material component is crushed moonstone.

GA p.56. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

name: Defense Against Nonmagical Reptiles and Amphibians

system.description:
A creature protected by this spell gains an edge in combat against non-magical reptiles and amphibians, including snakes, dinosaurs, frogs and giant kinds of such animals. Dragons and other creatures with unnatural abilities are not affected. Such animals suffer -2 to hit the protected creature, and it gains +4 on saving throws against reptile or amphibian venom. The material components are a bit of snakeskin and a dried frog's leg in a pouch of hardened leather.

GA p.57. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell gives some protection from insects, spiders and scorpions, including giant and unnatural kinds. They suffer -2 to hit the protected creature, and it gains +4 on all saves against insect or arachnid venom. It works against no more than 20 hit dice of creatures of all these kinds; if more attack, the spell ends. The material component is an insect trapped in amber.

GA p.57. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell makes one or more small flashes of lightning leap from the caster's fingertips at one or more opponents: one arc for every three levels of the caster, each doing 1d6 damage plus one point per level (save vs. spells for half). It works best with each arc aimed at a different opponent, since only one arc can strike a target per round; others striking the same target have no effect. The material components are a bit of fur and a glass rod.

GA p.57. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell summons a pair of shimmering violet phantoms that stay on either side of the mage and protect him from all attackers.

Shield-maidens: AC 4 (phantom chain mail and large shield); Move 12"; HD 3; hp 20; Dmg 1d6 (phantom spear); THAC0 16; AL N.

They stay close enough for their shields to help cover the mage: one maiden's shield gives -1 to the caster's armor class, or -2 if both cover the same side. They can guard the caster against attacks from different directions, but will never move more than 50 feet away, even if ordered to, and they follow the caster magically wherever he goes. The material components are a pair of small crystal shields tied with string to a miniature wooden figure of the caster.

GA p.57. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell helps protect a creature against all molds, slimes, puddings, oozes and other formless, primordial beings. Their attacks on it are at -2, and it gains +2 on its saving throws against them. Its flesh also strongly resists their corrosive attacks, counting as solid stone for that purpose. The spell absorbs up to 10d4 points of damage from slime before it collapses. The material components are a bit of food mold pressed between two flat stones and a pinch of diamond dust.

GA p.57. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed.

This spell summons a band of phantoms that look like shimmering outlines of violet light. They do their best to stay between the mage and his enemies, giving him the time and room to defend himself with spells. To most creatures they are solid and seem real; to the mage they are completely transparent and insubstantial, so his attack spells pass through them to strike enemies and do the defenders no harm, even if they are inside the spell's area.

The mage can summon one of four sets of defenders, each best suited to a particular setting, but must choose which when memorizing the spell:
